newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech gov't agrees to sell some healthcare assets.
newsitem.headline: Czech gov't agrees to sell some healthcare assets.

text.p: The Czech government approved a plan on Wednesday to sell off some assets of cash-strapped healthcare facilities and reduce the number of beds to help cut booming costs, Health Minister Jan Strasky said.
Strasky told a news conference that buildings worth some 500 million crowns would be sold, and 1.7 billion crowns in planned investment would be eliminated.
The government has been trying to stem the growing debt load of state hospitals, saying there was a number of unnecessary facilities.

Strasky said revenue from the sales would we be ploughed back into the sector. Some buildings with beds would be turned into social care homes under supervision of the social affairs ministry, he said.
The cabinet is still mulling widespread reform of the healthcare financing system.
Currently insurance companies pay doctors and hospitals for each procedure performed, giving no incentive to save on drugs or facility costs.
Some large state hospitals are facing bankruptcy lawsuits brought by creditors.
